risk_reasons: The change edits an auth-gate error path shared by 12 owner-facing API routes.
It replaces an existing test that pinned the wrong 401 behaviour, so a check changes rather than only gets added.
goal: Issue #1361: when requireRole rejects for a reason that is not an AuthError, the three owner gates re-throw instead of answering 401, so a genuine server fault surfaces as a real 5xx.
non_goals: Do not change the AuthError mapping; 401 and 403 responses stay byte-identical.
Do not catch and return an internal_error 500; the locked decision is to re-throw.
Do not change requireRoleOr401, requireAdminWithAal2, or any other auth gate.
Do not edit the four /api/locations routes or the eight dashboard routes that consume these helpers.
Do not add a logger or Sentry call; onRequestError in src/instrumentation.ts already captures an error that escapes a route.
user_visible_behavior: A signed-out or non-owner caller still receives the same 401 or 403 JSON body it receives today.
A caller that hits a server fault, for example a database outage, receives a 5xx instead of 401 Unauthorized.

The owner no longer reads a server fault as a permissions problem; the response is a 5xx, not "Unauthorized". (The review wave measured that no client of these routes branches on 401, so no auto sign-out chain existed — that earlier claim is withdrawn.)
Sentry records the fault through onRequestError; today the 401 hides it.
invariants: AuthError stays the single owner of the refusal vocabulary; only non-AuthError handling changes.
Every response the helpers still build keeps its no-store cache headers.
Invariant #8 is untouched: owner scoping by account_id does not change.
edge_cases: requireRole rejects with a plain Error, for example a database outage: the helper re-throws.
requireRole rejects with a non-Error value, for example a thrown string: the helper re-throws that value unchanged.
requireRole rejects with an AuthError carrying 403: unchanged, the helper returns 403.
No call site wraps either helper in a try block, so the re-thrown error escapes the handler and Next.js returns 500.
The multi-location 404 gate and the same-origin 403 gate run before auth and stay unchanged.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/locations/owner-route.ts:43-54 — the same file's assertSameOrigin catch re-throws a non-SameOriginError.
src/lib/auth/route-helpers.ts:86-110 — the doc comment that names this exact drift as a past bug.
test_seams: src/lib/locations/__tests__/owner-route.test.ts — mockRequireRole rejects and readOwnerForMultiLocationRoute is called directly.
src/lib/approval/__tests__/http-routes.test.ts — mockRequireRole rejects and requireDashboardReviewOwner is called directly.
src/lib/auth/__tests__/resolve-owner-scope.test.ts — mockRequireRole rejects and resolveOwnerScope is called directly.
tests_to_add: re-throws when requireRole rejects with a non-AuthError
re-throws a non-Error rejection value unchanged
re-throws a non-AuthError rejection instead of masking it as 401
re-throws a non-AuthError rejection instead of wrapping it as ScopeError 401
rollback_plan: Revert the single commit. The change is two edited catch blocks plus their tests. There is no migration, no feature flag, and no data change.
observability: Sentry captures the escaped error through onRequestError in src/instrumentation.ts.
Vercel logs move the status for a server fault from 401 to 500, which is the signal this fix exists to restore.
